scenes.line1: How does Kafka keep data safe?
scenes.say: How does Kafka organize and protect your data? What exactly are topics, partitions, and brokers?

scenes.label: Topic
scenes.sub: A named stream of records in Kafka.
scenes.say: A Kafka topic is just a named stream of records. Think of it as a logical channel where data flows.
Each topic splits into partitions—these are ordered, unchangeable lists of records. Every record gets a unique offset, which lets consumers track their place.
Brokers are the Kafka servers that store partitions. Replication means each partition is copied to multiple brokers, so your data survives hardware failures.

scenes.question: Is an offset unique across all topics?
scenes.right: No, offsets are only unique within each partition.
scenes.say: Watch out: offsets are only unique within a partition, not across all topics or partitions.
